transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, it burns when I pass water, and I keep needing to go much more often than usual. It's been going on for a few days now.
Could you tell me in your own words how much this is affecting your daily life, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines, or none that you know of?
It's making things awkward — I've stopped going to the residents' coffee morning in case I can't get to the toilet in time. As for medicines, one of the antibiotics gave me an itchy rash once.
Could you tell me what medicines you take regularly, and whether any of them have been started or changed recently?
I take a tablet for my thyroid every morning, and another one for my thin bones once a week. There's also a cream I use twice a week from the hospital, but I can't remember what it's called.
Besides the thyroid and bone tablets you mentioned, do you have any other long-term health conditions that a doctor has told you about?
The thyroid is one, and they told me I have thin bones, that's why I take the tablet for them. I don't think there's anything else.
How much are the burning when you pass water and needing to go more often affecting your day-to-day life at the moment — not at all, a little, a lot, or are you not sure?
The stinging's about a 5 out of 10, I'd say — uncomfortable, but I'm managing. It's the having to keep rushing to the toilet that's the nuisance.
When you pass water and it stings, whereabouts in your body do you feel that stinging?
It's down below, when the water comes out. That's when it stings.
Besides the stinging and needing to go more often, is there anything else you’ve noticed going on?
The water looks cloudy and smells stronger than usual. I haven't seen any blood in it, though.
What’s the main thing that worries you about all of this?
I think it's another water infection, like the one I had about a year ago. I'm hoping to get some antibiotics before the weekend.

Apart from the thyroid problem, the thin bones, and the water infection about a year ago, is there anything else about your past health—like other health problems, operations, or hospital stays—that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else like that. Just the thyroid, the thin bones, and that water infection a year ago.
Is there anything else you've noticed that you'd like to add?
No, I haven't had any fever or shivers, and my niece hasn't noticed me being muddled or anything like that.
Do you have any allergies to medicines, or have you ever had a bad reaction to a medicine?
Yes, it was trimethoprim — that's the antibiotic that gave me an itchy rash.
Could you tell me about any medicines you're taking now—either regularly or ones you've started recently—and the doses if you know them?
I take the thyroid tablet every morning and the bone one once a week, and the cream twice a week. I'm afraid I don't know the doses, sorry.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
